sections.h2: Where is the Barry County Register of Deeds, and what will staff do for you?
sections.html:
The office is in Room 102 on the first floor of the Barry County Courthouse, 220 W State Street, Hastings, MI 49058. It lists weekday hours of 8:15 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. with a lunch closing from noon to 1:00, a phone line at 269-945-1289 and the email bcrod@barrycounty.org. The county's own wording is worth repeating: recording a deed makes it public record, and it does not make the deed legal.

Staff will record, index and keep what you bring them, and they will not run a title search or advise on documents. The office keeps no blank forms, so a seller who needs a deed gets it from a title company or an attorney. A recorded paper cannot be edited later, which means an owner who wants a name added or removed signs and records a fresh deed.

The register's page also explains the difference between a deed and a title. Most houses have no separate title document, because the recorded deed covers everything permanently attached to the land. A few older mobile homes still carry a title filed with the Secretary of State.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Barry County, and who pays what?
sections.html:
Every document costs $30.00 to record regardless of page count, and a paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument number adds $3.00 for each extra one. Documents that sell or transfer real estate also owe state and county transfer tax at the time of recording. The recording fee and the tax can be paid together with one payment to the Barry County Register of Deeds.

One charge goes elsewhere. Warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts and land contract assignments need a Tax Certification from the Barry County Treasurer. That is $5.00, and it has to be a separate check payable to the Barry County Treasurer.

Barry County recording and copy charges (Barry County Register of Deeds)

Recording, any document$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3.00

Copy by mail or email$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 search fee if no document number

Cash, check, debit and credit are accepted, and card payments carry a small service fee.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax would a Barry County seller owe?
sections.html:
The register's FAQ says transfer tax runs $4.30 per $500 of consideration, that the seller pays it, and that it is due when the deed is recorded. On a $264,100 house, which matches the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value for Barry County, the price holds 529 blocks of $500 once the partial block is counted. That puts the tax at $2,274.70.

Exemptions exist, but staff cannot pick one for you. The deed has to cite MCL 207.505 for the county tax or MCL 207.526 for the state tax, together with the letter of the exemption claimed. The office keeps separate county and state exemption lists, and a closing agent or attorney should choose the right one.

  • A gift from a parent to a child, or to a grandchild, falls under the state exemptions.
  • A transfer by foreclosure or a deed in lieu of foreclosure is also exempt at the state level.
  • A deed that corrects a flaw by confirming title already held is exempt, as is an instrument showing a price under $100.

The full state list sits in MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Barry County office will accept it?
sections.html:
Michigan law sets recording standards, and the Barry office posts a checklist built on them. Check each item before you file. The list below paraphrases the main items from the county's page.

  • Original signatures in black or dark blue ink, with names typed or printed beneath them.
  • An acknowledgment by a Michigan judge, court clerk or notary, with the notary's name printed on the same page.
  • The grantee's street or post office address, and the name and address of whoever drafted the paper.
  • A top margin of at least 2.5 inches on page one and half an inch on every other side.
  • Legible black type of at least 10 point, on white paper of at least 20 pounds, between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • The total value of the property on the face of the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached.
  • A certified death certificate recorded with, or before, any deed that passes property to a survivor.

A copy of a document cannot be recorded. Court orders must carry the clerk's seal, and everything else needs the original signature.

sections.h2: How do you submit a Barry County deed, and how fast does it come back?
sections.html:
You can bring it to the counter, mail it, or send it through an e-recording provider. The county lists five providers: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, Nationwide Title Clearing, EPN and CSC. It does not record anything sent by plain email.

The FAQ says the office records a compliant document on the day it arrives. In-person filers leave with the recorded copy. Mailed or dropped-off papers usually return within 2 to 4 business days when a self-addressed stamped envelope is enclosed, and without one the office holds the paper for at least 90 days. Free digital PDF returns through Swift can be arranged with the office staff.

The county's page notes that the treasurer provides tax certifications electronically only through Simplifile and CSC, which matters if your title company prefers another provider. A seller rarely makes this choice, but the closing agent should confirm it before the signing date.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax, and what happens with a foreclosure or sheriff's deed?
sections.html:
Barry's register has no role in property tax. The FAQ sends owners to the city or township for current bills and to the Barry County Treasurer for delinquent tax. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure on any parcel with back tax before you set a closing date.

The office also does not hear about foreclosures until after the sale takes place, so it cannot tell you whether a house is scheduled for a sheriff's sale. Once a sheriff's deed is recorded, the office can accept the redemption fee, but it does not work out how much that is. A title search at one of the public workstations, or through a title company, shows open liens.

The county also recommends its GIS property map as a starting point for ownership questions. That map follows the tax roll, so it names the listed taxpayer. The recorded deed is what confirms who owns the parcel.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Barry County itself?
sections.html:
Barry County covers 577 square miles, of which 553 are land, and Hastings is both the only city and the county seat. The villages are Freeport, Middleville, Nashville and Woodland. Delton, Dowling and Hickory Corners are census-designated places. Kent County lies to the northwest, Kalamazoo County to the southwest and Eaton County to the east and Calhoun County to the southeast.

The county has no passenger rail. Its only line is a two-mile CSX section in the northeast corner of Woodland Township. Drivers use M-37 to reach Hastings from the north and south, M-43 through Delton and Hastings, M-79 from Nashville toward Hastings, M-66 along the eastern side and M-89 and M-179 in the west and southwest.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 63,991, a 2.5 percent increase over 2020.
  • Housing units in 2025: 28,284, and 24,480 households.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 87.3 percent, with a median value of $264,100.
  • Median household income: $77,500, and median gross rent: $972.
  • Mean commute: 27.7 minutes, and building permits in 2025: 157.

With a mean commute near 28 minutes, buyers here weigh drive time and condition. A house with deferred repairs can be hard to finance, and a cash buyer who purchases as-is offers a way to close without fixing them first.

faqs.q: What hours does the Barry County Register of Deeds keep?
faqs.a: The office lists Monday through Friday from 8:15 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., closed from noon to 1:00 for lunch. Hours can shift on holidays and special dates, so call 269-945-1289 before a trip.

faqs.q: Does Barry County record documents sent by email?
faqs.a: No. The register cannot record a document that arrives by plain email. Use an e-recording provider such as Simplifile, EPN or CSC, or bring or mail the original.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Barry County home sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays, according to the register's FAQ, and the tax is due when the deed is recorded. It comes to $4.30 per $500 of consideration, which includes $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county.

faqs.q: Can the Barry County office tell me who owns a parcel?
faqs.a: Not directly. Staff can only pull the last deed under a particular name, so start with the GIS property map to see the listed taxpayer, then search that name at the public workstations.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my recorded deed in Barry County?
faqs.a: Ask the office to mail or email one for $1.00 a page, plus a $5.00 search fee if you do not know the document number. Payment must arrive first, by check in the mail, since staff cannot take it by email or phone.
